arxiv-2210-08026.title: Magnetic-field-induced cavity protection for intersubband polaritons
arxiv-2210-08026.creator: Daniele De Bernardis 1 , Mathieu Jeannin 2 , Jean-Michel Manceau 2 , Raffaele Colombelli 2 , Alessandro Tredicucci 3 , and Iacopo Carusotto 1
arxiv-2210-08026.description: Abstract We analyse the effect of a strong perpendicular magnetic field on an intersubband transition in a disordered doped quantum well strongly coupled to an optical cavity. The magnetic field changes the lineshape of the intersubband optical transition due to the interface roughness of the quantum well from a Lorentzian to a Gaussian one.

The U.S. Government retains for itself, and others acting on its behalf, a paid-up nonexclusive, irrevocable worldwide li
arxiv-2307-05381.creator: Samudra Dasgupta 1 , 2 ∗ {}^{1,2^{*}} , and Travis S. Humble 1 , 2 † {}^{1,2^{\dagger}}
arxiv-2307-05381.description: Abstract Stable quantum computation requires noisy results to remain bounded even in the presence of noise fluctuations. Yet non-stationary noise processes lead to drift in the varying characteristics of a quantum device that can greatly influence the circuit outcomes. Here we address how temporal and spatial variations in noise relate device reliability to quantum computing stability.

arxiv-2404-16459.title: Impacts of Energetic Particles from T Tauri Flares on Inner Protoplanetary Discs
arxiv-2404-16459.creator: V. Brunn, Ch. Rab, A. Marcowith, C. Sauty, M. Padovani, C. Meskini
arxiv-2404-16459.description: Abstract T Tauri stars are known to be magnetically active stars subject to strong flares observed in X-rays. These flares are likely due to intense magnetic reconnection events during which a part of the stored magnetic energy is converted into kinetic energy of supra-thermal particles.

arxiv-2407-00099.title: Optimal Transport for Latent Integration with An Application to Heterogeneous Neuronal Activity Data
arxiv-2407-00099.creator: Yubai Yuan, Babak Shahbaba, Norbert Fortin, Keiland Cooper, Qing Nie, Annie Qu
arxiv-2407-00099.description: Abstract Detecting dynamic patterns of task-specific responses shared across heterogeneous datasets is an essential and challenging problem in many scientific applications in medical science and neuroscience. In our motivating example of rodent electrophysiological data, identifying the dynamical patterns in neuronal activity associated with ongoing cognitive demands and behavior is key to uncovering the neural mechanisms of memory.

arxiv-2410-01535.title: GaussianBlock: Building Part-Aware Compositional and Editable 3D Scene by Primitives and Gaussians
arxiv-2410-01535.creator: Shuyi Jiang, Qihao Zhao, Hossein Rahmani, De Wen Soh, Jun Liu, Na Zhao
arxiv-2410-01535.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shuyi Jiang, Qihao Zhao, Hossein Rahmani, De Wen Soh, Jun Liu, Na Zhao. Recently, with the development of Neural Radiance Fields and Gaussian Splatting, 3D reconstruction techniques have achieved remarkably high fidelity. However, the latent representations learned by these methods are highly entangled and lack interpretability. In this paper, we propose a novel part-aware compositional reconstruction method, called GaussianBlock, that enables semantically coherent and disentangled representations, allowing for precise and physical editing akin to building blocks, while simultaneously maintaining high fidelity.

pmc-11639271.title: Optimal wideband digital fractional-order differentiators using gradient based optimizer
pmc-11639271.creator: Mohammed Ali Mohammed Moqbel, Talal Ahmed Ali Ali, Zhu Xiao
pmc-11639271.description: In this paper, we propose a novel optimization approach to designing wideband infinite impulse response (IIR) digital fractional order differentiators (DFODs) with improved accuracy at low frequency bands. In the new method, the objective function is formulated as an optimization problem with two tuning parameters to control the error distribution over frequencies.

pmc-11712103.title: Polytreatment in a very old patient. What’s better for safe prescribing?
pmc-11712103.creator: Pietro Gareri, Ilaria Gareri, Luciana Barbara Covello, Manuela Ammendola
pmc-11712103.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPrescription for inappropriate drugs can be dangerous to very old people, due to the increased risk of adverse drug reactions.Case reportWe report the consequences of inappropriate prescriptions in a 99‐year‐old woman. She had a clinical history of vascular dementia, diabetes, hypothyroidism, heart failure, osteoarthritis, chronic renal failure, and hypoacusia, and was admitted to our attention for asthenia and loss of appetite. She was hospitalized two months before for third‐degree atrioventricular block, and underwent pacemaker implantation.

pmc-13373218.creator: B. Navashreya, Narasimha Raju Chebrolu, I. V. Sankar, Aalu Boda

pmc-13486637.title: Proximity in mice induced by an auditory-conditioned stimulus
pmc-13486637.creator: Wataru Ito, Alexei Morozov
pmc-13486637.description: Social affiliation promotes survival and well-being across species, and proximity to conspecifics is a necessary precondition for affiliative contact. While innate threats reliably increase proximity among conspecifics, whether learned threats have the same effect remains unknown. Here, we report that an auditory conditioned stimulus (CS) induces proximity in mice.
